rules.statement: Keep a try block around only the operation its catch's log message names; run follow-up work such as per-item cache evictions outside it, or give that work its own try with a log message that names it.
rules.why: A broad try logs a failure in follow-up work under the wrong message, which points operators at the wrong component, and it stops the loop at the first failing item.
rules.check: Look for a catch whose log message describes one operation (e.g. reading data) while its try also wraps other calls such as removals or a loop over items; check whether one failing item aborts the rest.

rules.statement: When a loop applies a best-effort operation to each item, handle each item's failure on its own, log it naming the item, and continue with the remaining items instead of aborting the loop.
rules.why: Stopping at the first failure leaves the other items unprocessed, and a fallback that runs afterwards hides the real error.
rules.check: Look for loops over items whose per-item call can throw and whose exception escapes to an outer catch, ending the loop early without logging which item failed.

rules.statement: Create a Dictionary, List or HashSet with an initial capacity when the maximum number of entries is known up front, such as the count of the source collection.
rules.why: Without a capacity the collection may resize several times while it is filled.
rules.check: Look for `new Dictionary<...>()`, `new List<...>()` or `new HashSet<...>()` filled from a collection whose Count is available, without passing that count as the capacity.

rules.statement: In a test project, when a change deletes a test for a failure path, add a test that still covers that path, such as every fallback call throwing at once.
rules.why: Without it, a regression where that failure starts escaping would leave the suite passing.
rules.check: Compare deleted test methods with the added ones; flag a removed failure-case test (e.g. both clears failing) whose scenario no new test covers.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't prove that an async operation is still waiting by sleeping with `Task.Delay` and then asserting it hasn't completed; assert it is pending right after it starts, or use a deterministic gate, then trigger completion and await it under the test's deadline.
rules.why: A timing check proves little about the wait and makes the test slower and flaky.
rules.check: Look for `Task.Delay(...)` or `Thread.Sleep` in tests followed by an assertion that a task is not completed.

rules.statement: In a test project, end every Moq `Setup`/`SetupGet` on a strict mock with `.Verifiable()`, including setups in helper methods, and create mocks from the test's MockRepository when there is one.
rules.why: Otherwise, if the code under test stops using a setup, no verification catches the unused setup.
rules.check: Look for `Setup(...)`/`SetupGet(...)` chains without `.Verifiable()`, and `new Mock<T>(MockBehavior.Strict)` created outside the test's MockRepository.

rules.statement: Re-wrap an XML doc comment paragraph to the file's usual 120-column width after editing it, keeping its words unchanged.
rules.why: Inserted sentences leave lines unevenly wrapped and running past the paragraph's wrap width.
rules.check: Look for edited `///` comment paragraphs where one line runs well past 120 columns or the wrapping is uneven.

rules.statement: Don't cite an ADR or coding rule as binding in a finding unless it exists in this repository's decision records or instruction files; check that it is there before reporting a violation of it.
rules.why: The maintainer declined a finding that cited an ADR and a bounded-channel rule that the repository does not have.
rules.check: Before citing an ADR number or named rule, confirm it exists in the repository's docs/decisions folder or its C# instruction files.

rules.statement: Don't flag an in-memory coalescing set used as a work queue as an unbounded queue when its size is bounded by the number of distinct keys, not by the request rate, it drops nothing, and its documentation says so.
rules.why: Its memory is bounded by the number of distinct keys, so the concern about an unbounded queue does not apply.
rules.check: Check whether the collection deduplicates by key, so that repeated requests for the same key coalesce, and whether the class summary explains the bound.
